biteOfDay: Stocked rainbows on Taneycomo stay aggressive in the seams during low flows, with more browns becoming active as we move into October. On Table Rock, bass continue shifting from summer shallows toward points, creek channels, and deeper structure in the clear conditions.

tableRock.clarity: Gin-clear near dam; verify arms locally

taneycomo.temp: Tailwater ~50–56°F (recent pattern — verify at the bank)
taneycomo.generation: ~7,650 cfs at 1 AM CT (recent 7,650–8,027 cfs late 9/30–early 10/1). Typical early-fall: low overnight/morning, stronger afternoon/evening. Call SWPA 866-494-1993 before you go.

species.name: Bass
species.technique: Topwater at dawn; deep spoon, shakey head, deep crank mid-day

species.name: Walleye
species.technique: Crankbaits, live bait (carried mid-summer pattern — not freshly guide-verified 07-21)

species.name: Crappie
species.depth: Deep timber & brush piles (James River/Long Creek arms)
species.technique: Small white or yellow jigs under deep-water docks

species.name: Trout
species.technique: Low-flow morning window; pink worms/jigs/midges; drift when generation heavy (Trophy Area nightcrawlers)

species.name: Bluegill
species.technique: Worms, small poppers — great for kids (mid-summer pattern carry)

species.name: Catfish
species.depth: Indian Point & near dam, shallows after dark
species.technique: Stink bait, hot dogs, cut/frozen bait — evening/night

tip: Capitalize on low morning flows on Taneycomo: wade or drift seams with a 1/16–1/8 oz micro jig (brown/black/white/sculpin) or zebra midge under an indicator. Heavier rigs when generation ramps. Call SWPA 866-494-1993.
